result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on convergence against the prior blocker in the runtime refresh path, plus the directly touched project-shell refresh surface and the new ambiguity called out by the implementor. Re-checked the production wiring, targeted refresh tests, and reran the story and epic gates.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: The fake immediate-success default is gone. `DefaultSourceRefreshService` now requires an injected hydration executor, `createApp` wires a production `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor` through the real provider-adapter registry, and focused route tests prove refresh calls the provider seam and does not mark a source hydrated when runtime hydration fails.

newFindings.title: Project-shell refresh can still promise recovery for project-scoped stale/not-hydrated sources that the backend now rejects as not refreshable
newFindings.evidence: The story/design says project-scoped actions appear in the project source section and Story 3 includes refresh/rehydration for `stale` and `not_hydrated` attachments. In the client, `renderSourceAttachmentSection()` renders refresh controls for any source whose hydration state is `stale` or `not_hydrated` regardless of scope (`apps/platform/client/features/projects/source-attachment-section.ts`). In the new runtime path, `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.resolveTargetProcessId()` returns `null` for project-scoped attachments unless exactly one current process references the source, and `refreshRecoverableSource()` then returns `kind: 'not_available'` with message `no single current process working copy owns this source attachment` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts`). The modified API tests only verify successful refresh for process-scoped attachments; no server or client test proves the project-scoped case or suppresses the project-shell control when the backend will 409. This leaves project-scoped recoverability behavior unresolved and can present a false recovery path on the project shell.

productionPathFindings: Production no longer uses the prior fake immediate-success executor: `createApp` now injects `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor`, and the focused API tests show refresh invoking real provider-adapter hydration methods and preserving non-hydrated state on runtime failure.

Production refresh now has a new scope ambiguity for project-scoped attachments: the backend requires exactly one current owning process, while the project-shell UI still offers refresh purely from `stale`/`not_hydrated` state, so some project-scoped rows can advertise a recovery path that immediately returns `SOURCE_ATTACHMENT_REFRESH_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
openQuestions: For a project-scoped source shown in the project shell, what should refresh target when zero or multiple current processes reference that attachment: select/create a runtime target automatically, or hide/disable refresh until a single target exists?
additionalObservations: The prior blocker is closed on the touched production path: settled refresh now depends on actual provider hydration/rehydration completion instead of an unconditional success stub.
No new fake adapter or shim remains in runtime code for the refresh execution itself; the remaining issue is a product/scope decision about project-scoped refresh semantics and UI truthfulness.
